## How the guide defines it

Not addressed in guide.

## How the guide uses it

On 48 pages, always about a specific named player and almost always about a quarterback. Paul Stone's Texas Tech bet turns on Will Hammond being ready after a torn ACL; Zach Cohen's John Mateer pick turns on a broken throwing thumb having derailed a Heisman campaign and the player now being at full strength; Stormy Buonantony dates Florida State's collapse to Jordan Travis's injury.

## Working definition — TTW DERIVED

The availability and physical condition of specific players, treated as a condition attached to a bet rather than as a rate.

## Why it matters — TTW DERIVED

It is the most common stated caveat in the guide. Several bets are explicitly conditional on a player being healthy, and the contributor says so rather than burying it.

## How bettors use it in this guide

Case by case, and forward-looking only where a known injury is resolving. The guide makes no attempt to forecast future injuries and prints no injury-adjusted rating.

## Where it appears

pp. 5–15 where injuries are attached to priced bets; p. 39 for the Mateer case; p. 45 for the quarterback feature.
